title: Preserve errors for fractional retry counts
body:
## Problem

When `retries` is a positive fractional number, the retry loop exits before the failure handler can enforce exhaustion. This replaces the operation's last rejection with the internal `Retry attempts exhausted without throwing an error.` fallback.

## Fix

Let the failure handler remain the single authority for retry exhaustion. It already uses `retriesLeft > 0` consistently for integer, fractional, and infinite retry counts, so the redundant outer loop condition and unreachable fallback are removed.

## Tests

- `./node_modules/.bin/ava --match='*fractional*' test.js` — passed (1 test)
- `npm test` — passed (XO, 71 AVA tests, TSD)
- `git diff --check` — passed

## Compatibility

Fractional numeric values remain accepted. The change preserves the original operation error and follows the existing positive-`retriesLeft` behavior; integer and infinite retry paths remain covered by the full suite.

## Related issue

No issue. Reproduced independently on current `main`; searches for `fractional retries` and the internal fallback message found no issue or PR.

title: Documentation for destructuring params of `options.onFailedAttempt` does not match `FailedAttemptError` parameter type.
body:
The documentation for the `options.onFailedAttempt` method specifies that its' parameters can be destructured like so:
```jsx
onFailedAttempt: ({error, attemptNumber, retriesLeft}) => {...}
```
When destructuring the `error` value, typescript returns this error: `typeProperty 'error' does not exist on type 'FailedAttemptError'.ts(2339)`.

Replacing `error` with `cause` satisfies the type, indicating that the example in the documentation should be updated to:
```jsx
onFailedAttempt: ({cause, attemptNumber, retriesLeft}) => {...}
```

title: p-retry + dynamic import() behave different in Node and browsers
body:
Recently, I am trying to use p-retry with dynamic import() functions.

Node and browsers have quite different implementation of `import()`: they throw different errors on failure.

Run the following code in node and browsers (foobar.js doesn't exist and always throw error):

```js
pRetry(() => import('./foobar.js'));
```

In Node.js 20, it throws the following error:

```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package '/Users/guo/git/test/foobar.js' imported from /Users/guo/git/test/test.js
```

Since it is not a TypeError, p-retry will retry as expected.

However, if you run the same code in Chrome 131, p-retry won't retry. Because import() throws TypeError on failure, and it is not recognized as network error by is-network-error package:

```
TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: http://localhost:3000/foobar.js
```

To enable retries, I need to modify my code to:

```js
pRetry(() => import('./foobar.js'), { shouldRetry: () => true });
```

title: Don't error when trying to extend non-extensible errors
body:
Before this change, `pRetry` blindly tries to modify the error thrown by the inner function. If that error happens to not be an extensible object, this modification itself throws, which aborts the retry chain and obscures the inner error. This change makes `pRetry` not add these properties if the error object can't be extended under the presumption that retrying this error is better than hard erroring the first time its thrown.

Fixes #25
